verses.1: And my father knew that there was a man from the family of Elimelech. His name was Boaz.
verses.2: And Ruth said to Naomi, “Please go into the field and find some food. After all, I have found favor in his eyes.” Then she said to her, “Go, my daughter.”
verses.3: And she went there, and entered the field. She fought among the enemies. A portion of the field was given to Boaz, who belonged to the family of Elimelech.
verses.4: And behold, Boaz came out of the granary. He said to the men, “The LORD is with you.” They replied, “May the LORD bless you.”
verses.5: And Boaz said to the young man who stood over the flocks, “To whom is this young girl belonging?”
verses.6: And the boy who was standing on the coals said, “The girl from Moab is the one who came back from the field of Moab with Naamim.”
verses.7: And Alkatna said, “I gathered them together in a place after the people had left. She came and stood there from morning until now. The house remained empty all that time.”
verses.8: And Boaz said to Ruth, “Do not go out into the field to gather crops. Also, do not leave this place. You shall stay with my daughters.”
verses.9: Your eyes were in the field where they were working. I didn’t tell the boys not to touch you. Instead, they went away and ate from what was left over by the boys.
verses.10: And she fell to her knees, and she bowed down to the ground. Then she said to him, “How can I find favor in your eyes? I am a foreigner.”
verses.11: And Boaz said to her, “Tell me everything you’ve done after your husband died. Your father and mother left you, and you left your homeland. You went to a people whom you didn’t even know.”
verses.12: May the LORD reward your efforts, and may your efforts be successful. May you be blessed by the LORD, the God of Israel, who has come to protect you under His wings.
verses.13: And she said, “O Lord, see that you have kindled in your eyes a feeling of compassion for me. For you have spoken from the heart towards your wife, and I will not be one of your wives.”
verses.14: And Boaz said to her, “At the time of eating, you shall eat from the grain. You shall wash your hands with water before eating. Then you shall sit by the side of the men who are going to marry. Kallie will feed you, and you will eat and be satisfied.”
verses.15: And he stood up to fight. He commanded his men, “Also among the trees, you must also fight. Do not let them escape.”
verses.16: And even though they were taken away from their homes, and you abandoned them, she will not be harmed. Do not hurt her at all.
verses.17: And they wandered in the wilderness until dawn. They searched for those who were lost. And it became like a place full of holes.
verses.18: And she went in and entered the city. She saw that it was burning. Then she went out and gave her what remained of the fire from the altar.
verses.19: And her sisters said to her, “Where will you go today? I hope that God will bless you.” Then she told her sisters what she had done with him. She said, “The name of the man I did this with today is Boaz.”
verses.20: And Naomi said to her daughter, “Blessed be He who did not abandon His kindness toward the living and the dead.” Then Naomi said to her daughter, “Naomi says that the man from our tribe is near us now.”
verses.21: And Ruth said, “Also, because he said to me, ‘Do you really want to keep all the harvest that I have?’”
verses.22: And Naomi said to Ruth, “Good is this! I will go with my daughters, and they will not harm you in any field elsewhere.”
verses.23: And Boaz clung to the young women, so that they would harvest all the wheat and barley crops. Then he settled down with them.
